items.stem: Iris recorded gross sales of $244,000, sales returns of $10,600, and sales allowances of $4,300. What amount should Iris report as net sales?
items.candidate_workload: Read 3-number scenario (gross, returns, allowances). Apply net sales formula: $244,000 - $10,600 - $4,300 = $229,100. Distractors test different subtraction combinations. Reading + calculation combined warrant Moderate-Easy.

items.stem: Zephyr bought equipment for $156,800, salvage $12,000, 5-year life. What is annual straight-line depreciation?
items.candidate_workload: Extract cost, salvage, life from narrative. Apply SL formula: ($156,800 - $12,000) / 5 = $28,960. Distractors test common errors (forgetting salvage, using wrong denominator). Moderate-Easy recognizes the formula-application demand.

items.stem: Xavier uses throughput costing. Per-unit costs: materials $20, labor $15, variable OH $10, fixed OH $8. What is the throughput cost per unit?
items.candidate_workload: Candidate must know throughput costing only includes direct materials ($20). Must resist including labor, variable OH, or fixed OH. Concept discrimination + calculation warrant Moderate-Easy.

items.stem: Hampton sells a product for $120 with variable costs of $45. Fixed costs are $300,000. What is the contribution margin per unit?
items.candidate_workload: Extract price and VC from scenario. CM = $120 - $45 = $75. Candidate must NOT subtract fixed costs from per-unit CM. Discriminator: fixed vs variable cost handling.

items.stem: Long scenario (~337 chars) with multiple conditions about asset impairment testing.
items.candidate_workload: Long scenario requiring substantial reading comprehension. Multiple data points to extract. Easy/1 understates the semantic parsing demand.

items.stem: Which of the following is considered a financial budget?
items.candidate_workload: Must distinguish financial budgets (cash, capital expenditure, balance sheet) from operating budgets (sales, production, materials). All 4 options are plausible budget types within the same domain. Moderate-Easy recognizes the discriminator challenge.

items.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of standard costing over actual costing?
items.candidate_workload: Candidate must evaluate 4 plausible advantages and identify the correct one. All options sound beneficial — requires genuine understanding of standard costing benefits vs actual costing. Moderate-Easy accounts for the comparative-analysis demand.

items.stem: Kestrel owns 30% of voting stock of an investee and can exercise significant influence. Investee reports net income of $120,000 and pays dividends of $40,000. What amount should Kestrel report as investment income?
items.candidate_workload: Equity method: recognize proportionate share of investee net income (30% × $120,000 = $36,000), not dividends. Candidate must know equity method rules and resist dividend-based distractors. Two-step concept application warrants Moderate-Easy.

summary: All 8 sampled items show clear evidence of under-labeling at Easy/1. Each requires scenario parsing, formula application, or concept discrimination that exceeds pure recall. Moderate-Easy/2 appropriately reflects the combined reading + computation + discrimination demand.

retained_vs_recalibrated.retained_easy: 600 items — correctly labeled at Easy/1 (84% of original 823)
